svg.title: Nihonga v1 architecture
svg.desc: The Qwen-Image-2.1 transformer with 32 slots: blocks 5 and 20 are replaced by bridges, shown in detail (an 8-head attention branch with its own prompt cache, then a conditioned MLP); the other 30 blocks carry a fused rank-32 Lightning LoRA. Sampling uses 10 points of the 40-step schedule: three small steps, then seven large ones.

≈ 25.2M weights · 8 heads (an original block: 218M · 32 heads)
The Lightning LoRA (fused)
A LoRA learns a thin correction beside a frozen
matrix: W·x + B·(A·x), with B 4,096 × 32 and A 32 × 4,096.
Ours: q, k, v and out of the 30 blocks, 31.5 M weights.
Step distillation: one LoRA step is trained to land
where five steps of the pruned model’s own 40-step
path land, on 1,000 prompts; letter tokens, found by
OCR, count ten times in the loss.
Fused after training: W′ = W + B·A.
No extra weights, files or time.
The 10-step schedule
